description.text:
Warning! This protocol is EXPERIMENTAL and under active development.
It may change at any time, including in backward-incompatible ways,
without incrementing the interface major version and without prior
notice. No compatibility guarantees of any kind are provided. Clients
and compositors must track the upstream definition in treeland-protocols
and must not rely on the current interface names, requests, events, or
semantics remaining stable across releases.

This extension allows a client to request that the compositor play
a window transition for a new window that opens from a specified
rectangular area, and, when the window is closed, transitions back
to that same rectangular area.

The rectangle is attached to an xdg-activation-v1 token string after
the token is committed, so the compositor can associate the rectangle
with the originating surface and use it as the animation source when
the target window appears.

The client may call set_geometry multiple times to update the
geometry, and the compositor uses the latest set geometry for both
the open and the close animation.

Optionally, the client may attach a live source surface to the
rectangle via set_source_surface. When a source surface is set, the
compositor uses its content as the source of the transition instead
of an empty rectangle, and renders it live while the transition is
playing.

The client may temporarily disable the rectangle by setting a
geometry of 0x0 size (zero width and zero height). While the
rectangle is disabled, the compositor does not use it as the
animation source or target and behaves as if no rectangle were
set, but the rectangle object and its association with the
activation token remain alive. The client can re-enable the
rectangle later by setting a positive size again; the target
window uses the latest set geometry whenever the rectangle is
enabled.

The full flow is:
1. A, the originating surface, obtains an xdg_activation_token_v1,
calls set_surface to identify itself, and calls commit to obtain
the token string.
2. A calls get_window_transition_rect on this manager, passing the
token string.
3. A calls set_geometry on the resulting rect object to define the
transition rectangle (relative to A), and optionally calls
set_source_surface on the rect object to attach a live source
surface for the transition.
4. A passes the token string to B, the target window.
5. B calls xdg_activation_v1.activate with the token and B's surface.
6. The compositor looks up the rectangle associated with the token,
converts it to global coordinates using A's position, and plays
the open animation from that rectangle to B's geometry.
7. While B is alive, A may call set_geometry again on the rect
object to update the transition rectangle. The compositor uses
the latest set geometry when B is closed.
8. When B is closed, the compositor plays the close animation from
B's geometry back to the rectangle.
9. Once the compositor stops using the rectangle, it sends the
closed event on the rect object. A destroys the rect object
after receiving this event.
10. If A destroys the rect object before B is closed (or if A's
client disconnects, or if A is destroyed), the compositor falls
back to its default animation.

Timing and responsibilities:

The client must call xdg_activation_v1.activate on the target
surface before that surface is first mapped (i.e. before the
wl_surface.commit that causes the compositor to map it). This
ensures the compositor has the transition rectangle available when
the surface appears.

The terms "must", "must not", "should", and "may" in this document
are to be interpreted as described in RFC 2119.
description.summary: window open/close transition relative to a rectangle

description.text:
This interface is a manager for creating window transition
rectangle objects. A window transition rectangle is attached to
an xdg-activation-v1 token string to request that the compositor
play a window transition from that rectangle when the token is
used to activate a new window, and back to that rectangle when
the window is closed.

Creates a new window transition rectangle object associated
with the given activation token string.
description.summary: create a window transition rectangle for a token

args.name: token
args.summary: the committed activation token string to attach the rectangle to

description.text:
Represents a rectangle that the compositor uses as the
reference area for window open and close animations. The
rectangle coordinates are relative to the surface that was set
on the associated activation token via set_surface. The
compositor combines the surface's position with the rectangle
offset to determine the global animation area.

The object remains live: the client may call set_geometry again
to update the rectangle, and the compositor will use the latest
set geometry for the close animation when the target window is
closed.

When the client destroys this object (or the client
disconnects, or the originating surface is destroyed), the
compositor falls back to its default close animation for the
target window.

Destroying the rectangle object removes the animation
association. If the target window is still alive, the
compositor will use its default close animation when the
window is closed.

Sets the rectangle geometry, taking effect immediately. The
x and y coordinates are relative to the surface set on the
associated activation token via set_surface. This request
may be called multiple times to update the geometry.

A geometry with a positive width and a positive height is
guaranteed to be valid. A width and height of both 0 is
also guaranteed to be valid and temporarily disables the
rectangle. Otherwise might be rejected with the
invalid_geometry error.

args.name: x
args.summary: x offset relative to the originating surface

args.name: y
args.summary: y offset relative to the originating surface

description.text:
Sets the surface whose content the compositor uses as the
source of the transition for this rectangle. The surface is
rendered live while the transition is playing; its content is
scaled into the rectangle set via set_geometry.

The surface must not already be in use for any other purpose,
and the compositor reserves it for use as a transition source
only: it is not displayed anywhere else, and the client must not
use it for any other purpose. A surface that has previously been
used as a transition source may be used again.

The client should keep the surface alive, and keep valid
content on it, while it is set as the source.

Passing null clears the source surface. The client may
replace the source by passing another surface; a previously
set surface is no longer used as a source. Destroying the
rect object or the surface itself also ends its use as a
source.

A surface that cannot be used as a source, for example one
that is already in use for another purpose, or that belongs to
another client, raises the invalid_surface error.
description.summary: set the live source surface used by the transition

args.name: surface
args.summary: the live source surface, or null to clear it

description.text:
Sent when the compositor is done with this rectangle. The
client must destroy the rectangle object after receiving this
event.

This is a notification only. No further events are delivered
on this object after closed.
description.summary: the rectangle is no longer usable

entries.name: invalid_geometry
entries.summary: the geometry cannot be handled by the compositor

entries.name: invalid_surface
entries.summary: the source surface cannot be used as a transition source
